cpu: Intel Core i7-10700 (8 cores / 16 logical processors), 64 GiB RAM
methodology: Six independent fresh Windows QPA processes, sequentially without a concurrent build/test. Each runs the actual MainWindow/DocumentTab/EditorView and application bindings, without dictionary resources or main() platform integration. Native window is active/exposed at validation points. An independent producer posts synthetic Qt input at fixed cadence, bypassing Windows input dispatch. Paint completion is a completed QWidget paint event, not compositor/display presentation. Normal draft timers and theme animations run; user settings/files are isolated; autosave and update checks are disabled. Timers: 8ms GUI heartbeat, 20ms working-set sampling. Perf scopes and event logging are enabled. Nearest-rank quantiles, 80 operations per continuous phase, 12 alternating theme actions (6 per theme), 2 first activations with deferred themes. p99 equals max for these small samples; not a population latency guarantee. Coalesced operations share the first completed viewport paint after dispatch returns; an operation that paints synchronously records its last nested viewport paint instead. A tab switched away before its first paint is reported as inputs_without_paint; paint quantiles exclude it. Working sets and sampled maxima are not heap sizes or guaranteed peaks.
